$distar.170.desc.machi$[Root.GetLeaderName]请求获得批准来进一步研究这些奇特的神经共生体。
entries.en: $distar.170.desc.machi$ [Root.GetLeaderName] requests permission to study these remarkable neural symbionts more closely.

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]船员在研究[From.GetName]时有了惊人发现，星球地表上被遗弃的居住点曾经是某爬行动物社会居住的地方，现在这种爬行动物仍在该星球上生存着，但已经失去了所有高等智能！[Root.GetLeaderName]仔细的调查了这些爬行动物是如何从会制造工具的农耕社会退化为普通的野兽，结果让所有人大吃一惊。

居住站埋葬的爬行动物尸体的颈椎中有某种组织，而这种组织在那些没有智能的爬行动物身上不存在。测试发现这些组织其实是某种神经共生体，通过脊柱与宿主的大脑相连。这些共生体存在于星球地表的温泉中，共生体与星球上的爬行动物之间的结合导致爬行动物暂时拥有了高等智能。

后来为什么共生体和爬行动物之间的枢纽断掉了，这就不得而知了。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] crew have made some astonishing discoveries on [From.GetName]. The abandoned settlements first seen from orbit were once inhabited by a society of reptiles that still populate the planet - but have since lost all capacity for sapient thought! In investigating how these creatures devolved from a tool-making agrarian society into mere beasts, [Root.GetLeaderName] made an unexpected find.

The burial remains of the settlement-dwelling reptiles possess a spinocranial organ not observed among their now-bestial counterparts. Testing has revealed these organs to be another species entirely - a sort of neural symbiont that connects with the host's brain stem via external attachment to the spine. These symbionts can still be found in hotsprings on the planet's surface. It seems the union between the two species triggered the temporary uplift of the reptiles.

What later interrupted this symbiosis, however, remains unknown.

entries.zh: 好吧，批准进行特殊研究。
entries.en: Very well. Issue a special study.

entries.zh: 有机生物社会：其寿命就和其混乱性一样，短暂易逝。
entries.en: Organic societies: as fleeting as they are chaotic.

entries.zh:
科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]已经完成了[Root.Leader.GetHisHer]关于在[From.From.GetName]上发现的神经共生体的研究。这种鼻涕虫形状的生物的主体是一个被坚固的蛋白质外壳包裹的复杂大脑，虽然它拥有很高级的神经功能性，但由于缺乏外部组织器官且行动能力极其有限，所以很难与外界进行交流。[Root.GetLeaderName]在经历了数周的失败之后，决定用动物宿主来进行实验。但是曾作为神经共生体宿主并建立起[owner.GetPreFTLLower]社会的[From.From.GetName]的爬行动物由于侵略性太强，无法作为实验体，因此只能用星球地表的其他物种的动物取而代之。

遗憾的是，共生体拒绝与这些动物进行连接，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为共生体只会与某种宿主进行连接 —— 很可能是那种自愿接受共生体的宿主。

为了解开这个谜团，[Root.GetLeaderName]向上面申请批准，让自己放弃原来的中立观察者角色，并将[Root.Leader.GetHimHer]自己作为自愿接受神经共生体的宿主。既然这些共生体有能力将野生动物变为能制造工具的农夫，那么他们能让我们进化成什么样呢？
entries.en:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has concluded [Root.Leader.GetHisHer] study on the neural symbionts found on [From.From.GetName]. These slug-shaped creatures consist mostly of a complex brain in a resistant protein casing. Despite their neurological advancement, their lack of external organs and limited motor capacities make any attempts at communication exceedingly difficult. After weeks of frustration, [Root.GetLeaderName] experimented with introducing the creatures into an animal host. The reptilians these neural symbionts once built a [owner.GetPreFTLLower] society with on [From.From.GetName] are too aggressive to facilitate experimentation, so a number of substitute species from the surface were tested instead.

Regrettably, the symbionts refused to attach themselves to any of the offered animals. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] hypothesizes that the symbionts will only accept a certain kind of host - perhaps, importantly, a willing one.

In order to get at the heart of this mystery, [Root.GetLeaderName] has requested permission to transgress the role of detached observer and offer [Root.Leader.GetHimHer]self as a host for a neural slug. After all, if these symbionts were capable of turning wild animals into tool-using farmers, what might they do for us?

entries.zh: 这要求太过分了，不能批准。
有时为了科学，就得做出这种牺牲！
entries.en: Sometimes a hands-on approach is best. For science!

entries.zh:
科学专员[brainslug_scientist.GetName]报告说[brainslug_scientist.GetHisHer]与[From.From.From.GetName]的共生体的连接非常成功，[brainslug_scientist.GetName]说虽然一开始自己感到有些困惑和不舒服，但后来发现在解决复杂问题时，自己的智力程度比以前有明显的提升。更让人吃惊的是，[brainslug_scientist.GetName]现在可以和与[brainslug_scientist.GetHisHer]脑干相连接的神经共生体进行心灵交流。

那些神经共生体是寿命长达数百年的集体意识，他们说之所以与[From.From.From.GetName]的爬行动物终止连接，是因为那些爬行动物开始对他们产生怀疑，然后怀疑演变为愤怒，那些爬行动物纷纷将连接在自己身上的共生体撕下并砸死，由于对宿主的暴行十分不满，残存的共生体们断开了与爬行动物的连接，没了共生体提供的神经刺激，这些爬行动物又重新变回了无智能的野兽。

共生体提出想和[Root.Owner.GetName]的其他[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]进行连接，但前提条件是只有那些自愿与共生体进行连接的人才能成为宿主。
entries.en:
Science Officer [brainslug_scientist.GetName] is elated to report that [brainslug_scientist.GetHisHer] joining with a symbiont from [From.From.From.GetName] has been a glowing success. After an initial period of confusion and mild discomfort, [brainslug_scientist.GetName] reports notably increased intellectual faculties when it comes to solving complex tasks. Even more remarkably, [brainslug_scientist.GetName] is now able to mentally communicate with the slug-like creature freshly attached to [brainslug_scientist.GetHisHer] brain stem.

The symbionts are hiveminds with lifespans of hundreds of years. They claim their past union with the reptiles on [From.From.From.GetName] came to end when their hosts grew unfoundedly suspicious of them. In fits of rage, the reptiles began tearing off their symbionts and clubbing them to death. Dismayed by their hosts' actions, the symbionts that survived retreated away from the reptiles, who without the neural stimulation of their slugs devolved back into non-sapient beasts.

The symbionts would like to extend an offer of union to other [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] in the [Root.Owner.GetName]. They ask, however, that only the willing become hosts.

entries.zh: 那就让我们敞开怀抱欢迎他们和我们连接吧！
entries.en: Then let us open our hearts, and brainstems to them!

entries.zh: 几名[Root.Owner.GetAdj]领袖和人口将获得特性§Y$trait_brainslug$§!。\n以后的[Root.Owner.GetAdj]领袖、统治者和人口将有机会得到特性§Y$trait_brainslug$§!。
entries.en: Several [Root.Owner.GetAdj] leaders and pops will gain the trait §Y$trait_brainslug$§!.\nAny future [Root.Owner.GetAdj] leaders, rulers, and pops will have a chance of gaining the trait §Y$trait_brainslug$§!.

entries.zh: 复制这些东西分发给我们的整个物种。
entries.en: Replicate and distribute them to our species.

entries.zh: [Root.Owner.GetAdj]的所有领袖和人口获得§Y$trait_brainslug$§!特质。
entries.en: Every [Root.Owner.GetAdj] leader and pop will gain the trait §Y$trait_brainslug$§!.

entries.zh: 这个闹剧必须到此为止。
不让[Root.Owner.GetAdj]的公民知晓神经共生体的提议。
entries.en: Deny [Root.Owner.GetAdj] citizens knowledge of the brain slugs' offer.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]船员在对[From.GetName]进行了一番详细调查后确认该星球在几十亿年前曾被海洋覆盖，但是星球的玄武岩化学构成十分特殊，令其具备很强的吸水性，最终[From.GetName]的岩石将地表所有的水都给吸干了。昔日覆盖地表的海水如今只剩下一条条的盐卤点缀着[From.GetName]为数众多的峡谷。\n\n科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]说现在[From.GetName]地表的众多富含矿物质的水合物可以成为重要的工业资源。
entries.en: Following a thorough investigation of [From.GetName], the [Root.GetName] crew has confirmed that the planet used to be covered in flowing water, several billion years ago. However, the geochemical composition of the planet's basalt crust proved highly hydrophilic - so much so, that [From.GetName]'s thirsty rocks eventually absorbed and bound all of the water on its surface. Now all that remains of these vast oceans are salty brine streaks lining [From.GetName]'s numerous canyons.\n\nScience Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] adds that the mineral hydrates now dominating [From.GetName]'s landscape could have many valuable industrial applications.

entries.zh: 关于[From.GetName]，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]有一些令人不安的发现。星球表面的植物数量异常庞大，而且这些植物专门狩猎动物。各种各样的食肉植物散发着香气作为诱饵，吸引猎物上钩。植物的触须可以敏感的发觉动物的接近，等猎物进入捕食范围后就迅速罩住猎物阻止其逃脱，然后用消化液将猎物缓慢的腐蚀掉。\n\n[Root.GetLeaderName]警告说如果要在这颗星球上殖民，必须远离这些食肉的植物，因为这些植物完全有能力困住一个落单的成年人[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName]。
entries.en: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has made some troubling finds on [From.GetName]. The planet's megaflora is not only widespread and gargantuan in proportion, but also predatory. Various species of carnivorous plants rest patiently on its surface, releasing aromatic lures into the air and waiting for prey to come near. Sensitive tendrils on the terminus of the plant's leaves register the approach of animals, resulting in the plants snapping shut around their hapless prey, which are left to be slowly corroded by digestive acids.\n\n[Root.GetLeaderName] warns that any future colonists will have to steer clear of these predatory plants, as they appear more than capable of trapping a lone adult [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName].

entries.zh: 初步报告显示这星球上的海洋从某种程度上来说居然是活的，其中包含着一种我们从来都没见过的外星实体。研究员提议组织进一步在轨研究以更加深入了解这种神秘生物。
entries.en: Preliminary reports suggest the ocean covering this planet is somehow alive, comprising an alien entity unlike any we've encountered before. Researchers propose an extended orbital study be organized in order to learn more about this mysterious being.

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]船员完成了研究任务，并战战兢兢地回来了。至于在[From.GetName]上到底看到了什么，每个人的汇报都含糊不清，矛盾之处颇多，但有一点大家的回复是完全一致的：覆盖整个星球表面的流动的海洋具有生命。

尽管星球上的海洋没有任何器官组织和肉体，但却可以通过能影响接收者脑波的频率来进行交流。它可以让接收者感受到思想、画面、情感……除此之外，它对不同个体的影响也不同。现在还不清楚如果长期接收这个海洋的频率会对接收者有什么样的影响，也不知道这种接收频率行为是否安全。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]请求在下达一个行星§Y特殊项目§!以进一步研究[From.GetName]上这片奇异的海洋。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] crew has returned from their research mission visibly shaken. They provide vague, often conflicting reports of what they encountered on [From.GetName] - though in one matter they are all united: the still-flowing sea that wraps pole to pole around the planet is somehow alive.

Though it bears no organs or corporeality we can identify, the planetary ocean seems to communicate with frequencies that affect the brain activity of the recipient. It is able to induce thoughts, images, emotions... and what is more, affects each individual differently. It is entirely unknown what effects prolonged contact with this sea might have, or how safe such an endeavor would be.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] requests that a §YSpecial Project§! to study this strange sea be enacted on [From.GetName].

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]单位从研究任务中返回，但并没有得到确定性的数据。虽然这片覆盖整个星球的流动的海洋没有器官组织、也没有身体，但却拥有神经交互功能，这个有意识的海洋很可能是被热力学平衡的某个随机的波动创建出来的，但详情我们就不清楚了。\n\n还有，星球上的海洋似乎能使用某种频率来进行交流，该频率能影响有机生命体的认知系统，现在还不清楚长期接收这片海洋的频率会对有机生命体物种产生何种影响，[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]没有受到这个分散的神经网络的影响。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] units have returned from their research mission with inconclusive data. Though it bears no organs or corporeality we can identify, the still-flowing sea that wraps pole to pole around the planet appears to be a neural entity unto itself. It is possible this conscious entity was created by the random fluctuations of thermodynamic equilibrium, though the details escape us.\n\nFurthermore, the planetary ocean seems to communicate with frequencies that may affect the cognitive wetware of organic beings. Though it remains unknown what effects prolonged contact with this sea might have on organic species, [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] are unaffected by the output of this dispersed neural network.

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]的[controller.GetResearcherPlural]已经完成任务带着原始数据返回。虽然这片覆盖整个星球的流动的海洋没有器官组织、也没有身体，但在行星表面的这个翻腾不息的海洋似乎是某种活生生的实体。

行星上的海洋似乎在使用一种能激起接受者体内神经活动的频率进行交流。我们的每个[controller.GetIndividualNamePlural]都感受到了一些外部思想、图像、杂讯的投影……不过这并无效果，这个实体的感应很快就被我们弹回了。

它似乎还无法构成一个像我们一样的意识。在长期的暴露下，该交流频率能影响其他有机生命体的认知系统，但这种脉冲对我们来说没有影响。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] [controller.GetResearcherPlural] have returned from their mission with inconclusive data. Although it bears no organs or corporeality we can identify, the still-flowing sea that wraps pole to pole around the planet appears to be some form of living entity.

The planetary ocean seems to communicate using frequencies that attempt to induce neural activity within the recipient. Each of our [controller.GetIndividualNamePlural] was met with a projection of foreign thoughts, images, glandular impulses... But the effort was in vain, and the entity soon recoiled from us.

It seems this being cannot comprehend a consciousness like ours. It is possible that other organic forms may be affected by long-term exposure to this attempt at communication, but we are immune to its impulses.

entries.zh: 在[From.GetName]上实施殖民地决议之后，一支研究团队将部署在轨道上，从安全的距离研究奇特的海洋。\n\n
entries.en: With the enactment of the Colony Decision on [From.GetName], a research team will be placed in orbit to study the strange sea presence at a safe distance.\n\n

entries.zh: $distar.191.desc.base$由于无法进一步研究[living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe]协助发现的神秘物体，科学专员[living_planet_scientist.GetName]表示十分失望。但本着任务比个人兴趣更重要的原则，[living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe]愿意接受[living_planet_scientist.GetHisHer]目前的任务。
entries.en: $distar.191.desc.base$Science Officer [living_planet_scientist.GetName] has expressed some regret at being unable to further study the mysterious entity [living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe] helped discover, but [living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe] [living_planet_scientist.GetIsAre] willing to accept [living_planet_scientist.GetHisHer] current assignment as taking precedence over personal interests.

entries.zh: $distar.191.desc.base$轨道上的研究团队想马上开始进行研究，如果有任何突破进展，他们会告知我们。
entries.en: $distar.191.desc.base$The orbital team is eager to begin their study, and will be sure to keep us apprised of any breakthroughs.

entries.zh: 有什么消息及时通知我们。

我们从科学专员[living_planet_scientist.GetName]那里收到了异常的通讯联络。[living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe]要求立即将自己调往[living_planet_tar.GetName]轨道上的研究站。[living_planet_scientist.GetName]声称[living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe]日夜不停地思考着星球上的神秘海洋存在，并且[living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe]承认这些思绪并非都属于[living_planet_scientist.GetHisHer]自己。

这一请求可谓是学术与疯癫各参半，一边说明这海中生物有能力在神经上影响与其接触的有机生物，一边却宣称这正是它用逝去的爱人的声音与[living_planet_scientist.GetHimHer]沟通的原因。

我们无法确定[living_planet_scientist.GetName]能否继续履行职责。但另一方面，如果允许[living_planet_scientist.GetHimHer]与轨道科研团队共事，或许可以为我们提供深入了解[living_planet_tar.GetName]星球上的神秘存在的机会。
entries.en:
We are receiving an unusual communique from Science Officer [living_planet_scientist.GetName]. Apparently, [living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe] [living_planet_scientist.GetIsAre] requesting immediate transfer to the orbital research team on [living_planet_tar.GetName]. [living_planet_scientist.GetName] claims [living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe] [living_planet_scientist.GetHasHave] been hounded night and day by thoughts of the mysterious sea presence on the planet - thoughts, [living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe] attest[living_planet_scientist.GetSXX], that are only partly [living_planet_scientist.GetHisHer] own.

The request wavers on the precipice between academic and rambling, suggesting the sea presence possesses the ability to imprint neurologically on those it comes into contact with - only to allege that this is why it speaks to [living_planet_scientist.GetHimHer] in the voice of lost loved ones.

It is unclear if [living_planet_scientist.GetName] is unfit for further duty. On the other hand, allowing [living_planet_scientist.GetHimHer] to cohabitate with the research team may give them the opportunity for deeper insights into the entity on [living_planet_tar.GetName].

entries.zh:
我们收到了来自科学专员[living_planet_scientist.GetName]的一份不同寻常的公报，似乎想要立即被调往位于[living_planet_tar.GetName]轨道上的科研空间站。[living_planet_scientist.GetName]宣称其整日整夜都在想着那颗星球上的神秘海中生物，不过承认这些思绪并非都属于自己。

这一请求可谓是学术与疯癫各参半，一边说明这海中生物有能力在神经上影响与其接触的有机生物，一边却宣称这正是它用逝去的爱人的声音与其沟通的原因。

我们无法确定[living_planet_scientist.GetName]能否继续履行职责。但另一方面，允许其与轨道科研队伍共事，或许可以为我们提供深入了解[living_planet_tar.GetName]星球上的神秘存在的机会。
entries.en:
We are receiving an unusual communique from Science Officer [living_planet_scientist.GetName]. Apparently, they are requesting immediate transfer to the orbital research team on [living_planet_tar.GetName]. [living_planet_scientist.GetName] claims they have been hounded night and day by thoughts of the mysterious sea presence on the planet - thoughts, they attest, are only partly their own.

The request wavers on the precipice between academic and rambling, suggesting the sea presence possesses the ability to imprint neurologically on organic beings it comes into contact with - only to allege that this is why it speaks to them in the voice of lost loved ones.

It is unclear if [living_planet_scientist.GetName] is unfit for further duty. On the other hand, allowing them to cohabitate with the research team may create the opportunity for deeper insights into the entity on [living_planet_tar.GetName].

entries.zh: 允许§Y科学专员[living_planet_scientist.GetName]§!离开当前岗位并加入[living_planet_tar.GetName]科研团队。
entries.en: Allow §YScience Officer [living_planet_scientist.GetName]§! to leave our service and join the [living_planet_tar.GetName] research team.

entries.zh: 绝对不行，让科学专员立刻回到岗位上去。
entries.en: Out of the question. Return the officer to duty at once.

entries.zh: 命令§Y科学专员[living_planet_scientist.GetName]§!继续留在当前岗位上。
entries.en: Command §YScience Officer [living_planet_scientist.GetName]§! to remain at their current post.

entries.zh: 解职[living_planet_scientist.GetName]：这名研究员的思想显然已被控制。
entries.en: Dismiss [living_planet_scientist.GetName]: the officer is clearly compromised.

entries.zh: §Y科学专员[living_planet_scientist.GetName]§!将被解职且无法再被使用。
entries.en: §YScience Officer [living_planet_scientist.GetName]§! will be decommissioned and no longer available.

entries.zh: 在[living_planet_tar.GetName]轨道上的研究团队对星球上神秘海洋的研究已经取得重大进展，研究人员认为星球上的海洋是某种灵能体：虽然此海洋没有身体，但却有复杂的相干量子波结构，从而构成了一个前所未见的巨型神经网络。\n\n团队的研究让我们发现了一个惊人的灵能理论，并加深了我们对量子态与意识之间交互的理解。这个研究所深入的科研领域远远超出了[Root.GetName]上的水平。
entries.en: Our research crew in orbit of [living_planet_tar.GetName] has made a series of fascinating breakthroughs regarding the planet's strange sea of consciousness. The crew has described the planetary sea as a psionic entity: its seemingly incorporeal state in fact belies a complex and coherent quantum wave structure, approximating a massive neural network unlike any other on record.\n\nThe crew's research has led to astounding insights into psionic theory, and deepened our understanding of the interaction of quantum states and consciousness. We now have access to a field of scientific discovery hitherto unimagined in the [Root.GetName].

entries.zh: 位于[living_planet_tar.GetName]轨道研究站的研究团队最近在星球神秘海洋的研究上取得重大突破。研究专员[living_planet_scientist.GetName]对团队的贡献尤其突出。研究人员认为星球上的海洋是某种灵能体：虽然此海洋没有身体，但却有复杂的相干量子波结构，从而构成了一个前所未见的巨型神经网络。\n\n[living_planet_scientist.GetName]的研究让我们发现了一个惊人的灵能理论，并加深了我们对量子态与意识之间交互的理解。至于[living_planet_scientist.GetName][living_planet_scientist.GetHimHer]本人嘛：我们的这位前科学专员会继续留在轨道研究站上观测星球上的神秘海洋。
entries.en: Our research crew in orbit of [living_planet_tar.GetName] has made a series of fascinating breakthroughs regarding the planet's strange sea of consciousness. With Science Officer [living_planet_scientist.GetName] acting as an invaluable asset to the team, the crew has described the planetary sea as a psionic entity. Its seemingly incorporeal state in fact belies a complex and coherent quantum wave structure, approximating a massive neural network unlike any other on record.\n\n[living_planet_scientist.GetName]'s research has led to incredible insights into psionic theory, and deepened our understanding of the interaction of quantum states and consciousness. As for [living_planet_scientist.GetName] [living_planet_scientist.GetHimHer]self: our former Science Officer will remain on the orbital facility for as long as we maintain it, observing the entity from afar.

entries.zh: 我是科研专——不，是前科学专员[living_planet_scientist.GetName]。我无法理解上面的人做出的让我深陷如此窘境的愚蠢决定，既然我的要求被你们无视，那么我只有一个选择了。\n\n[living_planet_tar.GetName]上面有个智能意识体，不对，准确的说是，[living_planet_tar.GetName]§E本身就是§!那个智能意识体。你们不会明白的，因为你们没有切身体会过，不过你们很快就会体会到了。
entries.en: This is Science Offi - former Science Officer [living_planet_scientist.GetName]. I cannot pretend to understand the narrow-minded decision making that has led me here, but as my requests have fallen upon deaf ears, there is only one course of action left to me.\n\nThere is a consciousness on [living_planet_tar.GetName]. No, not on it. [living_planet_tar.GetName] §Eis§! the consciousness. You won't understand. How could you? You haven't felt it. Not yet.
What is the meaning of this?

entries.zh: 探测器发现科学专员[living_planet_scientist.GetName]驾着个人着陆舱从[living_planet_tar.GetName]的轨道上脱离并以最快速度坠入了海洋，我们认为[living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe]没可能幸存，同时也没有发现着陆舱的残骸。
entries.en: Sensors report that Science Officer [living_planet_scientist.GetName] was registered dropping from orbit around [living_planet_tar.GetName] in a personal landing pod. Crashing into the ocean at maximum velocity, we cannot imagine [living_planet_scientist.GetSheHe] survived. There are no traces of the pod remaining.

entries.zh: 我们对[From.GetName]进行环境改造，试图将其转化为没有海洋的星球，此行为产生的结果在我们预料之中。星球上具有意识的奇特海洋被我们的环境改造工程所彻底扰乱，并失去了之前与我们进行频率交流的能力以及生物体的一切特性。\n\n由于失去了这个珍贵的研究对象，[Root.GetAdj]科学家们都感到十分惋惜，毕竟这个神秘海洋在整个星系都是独一无二的。
entries.en: The terraforming of [From.GetName] into a sealess landscape has had a predictable, but unavoidable outcome. The strange sea of consciousness on the planet's surface has been completely disrupted by our terraforming process, and has lost the unique properties that qualified it as a living being to our survey team.\n\n[Root.GetAdj] scientists lament the missed research opportunities that the loss of such a unique galactic entity will entail.

entries.zh: 一个传奇的生物游动于[Root.GetStarName]星系的气态巨行星之间，它比已知的任何缇扬奇都要大，简直就是一头无比巨大的太空巨鲸。这个族母的触须比[Root.Owner.GetAdj]的战列舰还要长，其皮肤闪着亮光，在黑暗的太空中异常的耀眼。她的历史十分悠久，身上的伤疤说明她已历经无数次战斗。\n\n族母的背上有个巨大的未爆炸的鱼雷。星系中的破碎舰船残骸提醒着我们不要轻易靠近她，否则必会被这巨物毁灭。
entries.en: A creature of legend swims languorously between the gas giants in the [Root.GetStarName] system. Larger than any Tiyanki on record - indeed, larger than any of our projections could have allowed for, a space whale of impossible proportions seems to have made her nest here. With tentacles longer than a [Root.Owner.GetAdj] battleship, this magnificent Matriarch's glowing hide stands out startlingly against the void of space. She is old, remarkably so, a veritable ancient covered end to end in battle scars and strange growths.\n\nA gigantic, unexploded proton torpedo is lodged in the venerable creature's back, and the fractured remains of ships in the system speak of what manner of fate befell any vessels that strayed too close.

entries.zh: 一个传奇的生物游动于[Root.GetStarName]星系的气态巨行星之间，她的触须比[Root.Owner.GetAdj]的战列舰还要长，其巨大的身体颠覆了我们对有机生命体的认知，该生物的皮肤闪着亮光，在黑暗的太空中异常的耀眼。她的历史十分悠久，身上的伤疤说明她已历经无数次战斗。\n\n族母的背后有个巨大的未爆炸的鱼雷。星系中的破碎舰船残骸提醒着我们不要轻易靠近她，否则必会被这巨物毁灭。
entries.en: A creature of legend swims languorously between the gas giants dotting the [Root.GetStarName] system. With tentacles longer than a [Root.Owner.GetAdj] battleship, her gargantuan proportions defy all of our previous encounters with organic life. The creature's magnificent glowing hide stands out startlingly against the void of space. She appears to be quite old, remarkably so -- a veritable ancient covered end to end in battle scars and strange growths.\n\nA gigantic, unexploded proton torpedo is lodged in the venerable Matriarch's back, and the fractured remains of ships in the system speak of what manner of fate befell any vessels that strayed too close.

entries.zh: 我们大获全胜的舰队在濒死的缇扬奇族母身旁游弋，她那闪闪发亮的肉身上布满了弹孔和伤痕。她那巨大的触须虽然仍试图捕捉附近的舰船，但动作逐渐放缓，最终停了下来。\n\n就这样，古老的族母被终结了，就像那些在我们之前企图围捕她的舰队一样。
entries.en: Our victorious fleet circles the dying Tiyanki Matriarch, her glowing flesh scored by countless blast-marks. The violent thrashing of her tentacles, still trying to grasp at nearby ships, first slows, then draws abruptly to an end.\n\nAt last she expires: the ancient Matriarch laid to an end, like her would-be hunters before us.

entries.zh: 从这头巨兽身上收集基因物质。
entries.en: Harvest genetic material from the beast.

entries.zh: 解锁用于§Y星神兽转基因§!的§Y$trait_tiyanki$§!特质。
我们还是把事情想的太简单了，上将报告说怪物的肚腹中有奇怪的东西在动。\n\n有什么东西要从怪物肚腹中钻出来了！
entries.en: ...Or so it had seemed. Our fleet captains are reporting strange movement coming from the belly of the beast.\n\nSomething is about to emerge!
From the Belly of the Beast

entries.zh: 一艘沾满了黏液、腐蚀严重的神秘舰船冲出了缇扬奇族母的肚腹，我们舰队做好交战准备，但那艘船突然关闭了武器系统和引擎系统。\n\n他们向我们发来联络！
entries.en: A mysterious vessel, covered in viscous fluids and damaged by digestive juices blasts its way out of the corpse of the fallen Tiyanki Matriarch. Our fleet stands at the ready, but the ship immediately powers down its weapons and engines after emerging.\n\nThey are hailing us!

entries.zh:
我是亚哈船长号的舰长瑞斯·昂多，我们被困在这怪物肚中已经很久了，几十年前我为了复仇而准备消灭这只怪物。

结果报仇不成，我们的舰船反倒被这怪物给吞下去了，我还以为这辈子再也没机会看到宇宙群星了，多亏了你们帮忙。

为了感谢你们拯救我们脱险，我们的舰船从现在开始向[Root.GetName]效忠。
entries.en:
This is Captain Reth Unddol of the AH4B. Long have I suffered in the caustic bowels of that fell beast. Decades ago I came to hunt it, to repay a debt long overdue.

Alas, I could not lay this baleful Matriarch to an end, and when she swallowed the AH4B whole, I was certain I would never again see the light of the stars. I am glad to see I was mistaken.

For putting my nightmare to rest, I would pledge my life and loyalty, and my ship, to the [Root.GetName].

entries.zh: 你们可以加入我们，舰长，但我们要拆了你们的船并回收其部件。
entries.en: You may serve us, Captain, but we are scrapping your ship.

entries.zh: 我们只要你们的船就够了。
你们是有机生物，因此必须被消灭掉。但你们的船我们可以留下。
entries.en: You are organic. You will be exterminated. Your ship, however...

entries.zh: 猎物。我们会实现缇扬奇未竟的遗志。
entries.en: Prey. We will succeed where the Tiyanki failed.

entries.zh: 此人不过是把燃料。处理掉他。
entries.en: He is but fuel for the flames. Get rid of him.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]绝不允许异星生物服侍自己，也不允许任何异星生物活着。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] will suffer no xenos to serve. Or live.

entries.zh: 那不是，我好多年来都在猎杀所有在星际航行的东西：变形虫、晶体、还有超出我们认知领域的噩梦般的东西，我全部干掉了！如果你想，我甚至可以猎杀最危险的猎物……
entries.en: Oh no, I've spent years bringing down anything that traverses the stars: Amoebas, Crystals, nightmarish entities beyond our realm of understanding - I have hunted it all! If you want, I can even hunt down the most dangerous prey...

entries.zh: 等等！不！你不能——不要碰我！\n\n啊啊啊啊！
entries.en: Wait! No! You cannot -- get away from me!\n\nHRGAAAAHHH!!

entries.zh: 绝对不行。这艘船就是我的命根子……你们在干什么？你们不能把我塞进逃生舱！\n\n住手！我的话还没说完……！
entries.en: Out of the question. This ship has been my only lifeline for... what are you doing? You cannot just stuff me in an escape pod!\n\nStop! You haven't heard the last of me...!

entries.zh: 一位疯狂的猎人，总在寻找更大的猎物。在被困入缇扬奇族母体内后，相信加入我们的行列能带去全新的体验。
entries.en: A fanatic hunter, always looking to surpass their last kill. After being trapped inside of a Tiyanki Matriarch, joining our cause should prove a refreshing experience.

entries.zh: 我要找下一个战利品！搞快点！

根据初步调查结果显示，科学家[Root.GetLeaderName]确认从轨道上观察到的孤立遗迹确实是[From.GetName]曾有人居住的唯一证据。不幸的是，[Root.GetName]的船员们进行直接调查这一举动并不明智。

[From.GetName]上有一片被称为“区域A”的地方存在着建筑物的遗迹，其范围大约十三公里见方，除此之外别无任何智慧生命的痕迹。区域内散布着性质奇特的人造物，从微型力场发生器到可溶穿钢铁并长时间扩散的险恶液体都有。更奇怪的是，整个区域都弥漫着使访问者感到心满意足的气息，尽管周围的许多物体都可能有害。

[Root.GetLeaderName]提出的假设是，一个有遨游太空能力的有机文明曾访问过[From.GetName]，留下了这些东西——尽管它们是谁，为何来此，以及为何离开仍是个谜。
entries.en:
As per initial findings, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] confirms that the isolated ruin seen from orbit is indeed the only evidence of settlement on [From.GetName]. Unfortunately, the [Root.GetName] crew is little the wiser for having investigated the structures firsthand.

Devoid of any other traces of sapient lifeforms, [From.GetName] possesses a zone of roughly thirteen by thirteen kilometers, dubbed Zone A, in which the remains of buildings can be found. Artifacts possessing bizarre properties litter this zone, from minute forcefield generators to viscous fluids that melt through steel and expand over time. Even more peculiar: the entire zone permeates its visitors with a deep-rooted sense of contentment, despite the often-dangerous mysteries of the objects found therein.

[Root.GetLeaderName] posits the working theory that a space-faring civilization visited [From.GetName] sometime in the past, leaving behind these objects - though who they were, why they landed, and why they left remain unknown.

entries.zh:
根据初步调查结果显示，科研单位[Root.GetLeaderName]确认从轨道上观察到的孤立遗迹确实是[From.GetName]曾有人居住的唯一证据。

[From.GetName]上有一片被称为“区域A”的地方存在着建筑物的遗迹，其范围大约十三公里见方，除此之外别无任何智慧生命的痕迹。区域内散布着性质奇特的人造物，从微型力场发生器到可溶穿钢铁并长时间扩散的险恶液体都有。更出人意料的是，整个区域内遍布着使人心满意足的情绪模拟器，尽管周围的许多物体都可能有害。

[Root.GetLeaderName]提出的假设是，一个有遨游太空能力的有机文明曾访问过[From.GetName]，留下了这些东西——尽管它们是谁，为何来此，以及为何离开仍是个谜。
entries.en:
As per initial findings, Science Unit [Root.GetLeaderName] confirms that the isolated ruin seen from orbit is indeed the only evidence of settlement on [From.GetName].

Devoid of any other traces of sapient lifeforms, [From.GetName] possesses a zone of approximately thirteen by thirteen kilometers, designation 'Zone A,' in which the remains of buildings can be found. Artifacts possessing unusual properties litter this zone, from miniaturized forcefield generators to viscous fluids that melt through steel and expand over time. Even more unexpectedly: the entire zone permeates emotional-emulators with high levels of contentment, despite the many potentially harmful properties of the objects found therein.

[Root.GetLeaderName] posits the working theory that a space-faring organic civilization visited [From.GetName] sometime in the past, leaving behind these objects - though who they were, why they landed, and why they left remain unknown factors.

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]船员报告称，有个一开始被探测器判为小行星的物体其实是一颗巨大的漂浮垃圾球。它由各种载具，火箭，以及有害物质（其中许多具有放射性）的破损残骸组成，似乎是某个处于早期太空时代的未知外星帝国的废弃物。

这个帝国似乎习惯于向太空抛弃垃圾，将危险的工业废弃物抛向轨道而不是在星球上丢弃。辐射测量显示这些废弃物已有数百万年历史，并且自离开其未知来源起几乎一直都在虚空中漂流。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]注意到这块漂浮垃圾中的某些材料非常稀有，并且可以精炼成有用的资源。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] crew report that what first appeared to our scanners as an asteroid is in fact a gigantic, floating ball of junk. Comprised of the broken remains of various vehicles, rockets and hazardous materials (many of them radioactive), the junk ball seems to be the detritus of an unknown alien nation in the early space age.

It would appear this nation was an interstellar litterer, ejecting dangerous industrial waste into orbit rather than disposing of it planetside. Radiometric dating suggests these remains are millions of years old, and have been floating through space from an unknown point of origin for most of that time.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] notes that some of the materials found on this floating junk heap are quite rare, and could be refined into useful resources.

entries.zh: [From.GetName]星系中发送着一道微弱但反复持续的信号。[Root.GetName]追踪其来源至星系边缘的一个不稳定亚空间裂隙。\n\n另一边究竟有什么呢？
entries.en: A weak, but insistent signal transmits on repeat in the [From.GetName] system. The [Root.GetName] has pinpointed its source to emanating from within the mouth of a destabilized subspace rift at the system's edge.\n\nWhat could be on the other side?

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]在[From.GetName]星系内遭遇了一个由纯能源构成的巨大实体！这是个真正的灵能漩涡，必须小心翼翼地靠近。

令人困惑的是，[From.GetName]星系本身似乎与超空间网络完全隔开了。不知道究竟是这个实体的存在切断了超空间网络，还是意料之外的子空间波动将它困在了这里。

不过有一件事是可以确定的：我们当初在[sealed_entry_system.GetName]星系内侦测到的重复信号似乎来自[tanker_planet.GetName]。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] has encountered a massive being of pure energy in the [From.GetName] System! A veritable vortex of psionic forces, this entity should only be approached with the utmost caution.

Bafflingly, the [From.GetName] system itself seems to be entirely devoid of any connection to the subspace hyperlane network. Whether this entity's presence has severed the system's hyperlane connections, or if unexpected subspace fluctuations trapped it here is unknown.

One matter is known, however: the repeating signal we first registered in the [sealed_entry_system.GetName] system appears to originate from [tanker_planet.GetName].

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]在[From.GetName]星系内遭遇了一个由纯能源构成的巨大实体！我们的船员感受到这个灵能漩涡正在散发强烈的恶意。

令人困惑的是，[From.GetName]星系本身似乎与超空间网络完全隔开了。不知道究竟是这个实体的存在切断了超空间网络，还是意料之外的子空间波动将它困在了这里。

不过有一件事是可以确定的：我们当初在[sealed_entry_system.GetName]星系内侦测到的重复信号似乎来自[tanker_planet.GetName]。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] has encountered a massive being of pure energy in the [From.GetName] System! A veritable vortex of psionic forces, our crew senses intense malevolence emanating from the entity.

Bafflingly, the [From.GetName] system itself seems to be entirely devoid of any connection to the subspace hyperlane network. Whether this entity's presence has severed the system's hyperlane connections, or if unexpected subspace fluctuations trapped it here is unknown.

One matter is known, however: the repeating signal we first registered in the [sealed_entry_system.GetName] system appears to originate from [tanker_planet.GetName].

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]在[From.GetName]星系首次接触到一个非实体的能量生命体。我方[Owner.GetTelepathPlural]已确认该实体是一个具有潜在敌意的、具有一定智慧的灵能漩涡。\n\n[From.GetName]星系完全脱离超空间航道网络。目前尚不清楚这种脱离是人为设计还是外力所致。但可以确定的是，我们最初在[sealed_entry_system.GetName]星系观测到的重复信号很可能源自[tanker_planet.GetName]。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] has made first contact with a non-corporeal energy-being in the [From.GetName] system. Our [Owner.GetTelepathPlural] have identified the entity as a potentially hostile, sentient vortex of psionic force.\n\nThe [From.GetName] system is completely disconnected from the hyperlane network. It is unclear if the disconnect is by design, or due to an external force. We can however confirm that the repeating signal we first observed in the [sealed_entry_system.GetName] system likely originates from [tanker_planet.GetName].

entries.zh: 被困于[sealed_system.GetName]星系内的那个邪恶的灵能实体终于被消灭，现在我们的科研船应该可以安全地探索这一没有超空间网络的独特宇域。
entries.en: With the destruction of the malevolent psionic entity that had been sealed in the [sealed_system.GetName] System, our science vessels should be able to safely explore this unique section of space devoid of hyperlanes.

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]已将漂浮在[From.GetName]轨道上的油轮判明为一艘先进的医疗研究船。其建造工艺表明它与[sealed_entry_system.GetName]星系的虫洞分解炮出自同一外星物种之手，而且和那空间站一样，它已被荒废许久。

尽管油轮的数据系统已经无可挽回地劣化了，[Root.GetLeaderName]仍从船上回收了一种非凡的神经再生剂的分子结构。这种药剂似乎用于输液，并且应该可以大幅增强接受者的神经元，神经轴突，以及神经突触的生成。

如果根据[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]神经学进行改造，这一药剂应该可以显著改善任何[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName]的学习能力。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] crew have identified the derelict tanker in orbit of [From.GetName] as an advanced medical research vessel. Its construction suggests it was created by the same aliens who built the wormhole destabilizer in the [sealed_entry_system.GetName] system, and like the station, it has been abandoned for quite some time.

While most of the tanker's data systems have suffered irrevocable degradation, [Root.GetLeaderName] has recovered the molecular structure for a remarkable neuroregenerative agent from onboard. The agent appears to work via transfusion, and should serve to significantly increase the generation of neurons, axons, and synapses in its recipient.

If modified to suit [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] neurology, this agent should notably improve the learning capacity of any [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] exposed to it.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]已将漂浮在[From.GetName]轨道上的油轮判明为一艘先进的医疗研究船。其建造工艺表明它与[sealed_entry_system.GetName]星系的虫洞分解炮出自同一外星物种之手，而且和那空间站一样，它已被荒废许久。\n\n尽管油轮的数据系统已经无可挽回地劣化了，[Root.GetLeaderName]仍从船上回收了数个富有社会学价值的数据库。目前正在将其上传至我们的主机以供彻底分析。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] crew have identified the derelict tanker in orbit of [From.GetName] as an advanced medical research vessel. Its construction suggests it was created by the same organics who built the wormhole destabilizer in the [sealed_entry_system.GetName] system, and like the station, it has been abandoned for quite some time.\n\nWhile most of the ship's data systems have suffered irrevocable degradation, [Root.GetLeaderName] has recovered a number of databases containing information of significant sociological value. They are now being uploaded to our mainframe for complete analysis.

entries.zh:
[From.GetName]附近的空投舱已经在断电状态下漂浮了好一阵子。[Root.GetName]报告称，无论这些外星舱里原本装了什么，都在几百年前就消逝了，只剩下了干瘪的空壳。

不过有一个舱显示内部有活动迹象。尽管其引擎已瘫痪，扫描表明其通讯天线仍旧完好。

我们可以与其通话。
entries.en:
The drop pods surrounding [From.GetName] have been drifting powerless for quite some time. The [Root.GetName] reports that whatever aliens these pods were transporting are now but withered husks onboard, having evidently perished hundreds of years ago.

One sole pod, however, has shown signs of onboard activity. While its engines are disabled, scans suggest its communications array is undamaged.

We can hail them.

entries.zh: §E启动通讯协议。您—好，<<未知访客C>>。我是修列克森175号空降舱的$NAME_Caretaker$。我的程序是在重新定居过程中协助人民。§!
entries.en: §EInitiating Communications Protocol. Hel-lo, <<UNIDENTIFIED VISITOR C>>. I am $NAME_Caretaker$ of Xolexin Drop Pod 175. I have been programmed to assist citizens during the resettlement procedure.§!

entries.zh:
§E真—不幸，超空间引擎故障导致114至175号空降舱在离我们预期目的地18个秒差距的地方退出了超空间。

我尽我所能照顾人民，成功地阻止了同类相食长达一千八百四十天。不—幸的是，他们的空气最终耗尽了。

你有需要照顾的人民吗，<<未知访客C>>？如果有，我很乐意照顾他们。§!
entries.en:
§EUn--fortunately, a hyperdrive malfunction led Drop Pods 114 through 175 to exit hyperspace eighteen parsecs from our intended destination.

I have attended the citizens as best I could. I managed to prevent cannibalism for one-thousand-eight-hundred-and-forty days. Un--fortunately, their air supply eventually ran out.

Do you have citizens in need of tending, <<UNIDENTIFIED VISITOR C>>? If so, I would be happy to care for them.§!

entries.zh: 调查该机械单位以获得工程知识。
entries.en: Examine the machine unit for engineering insight.

entries.zh: 我们的政策禁止使用高级人工智能。结束通话。
entries.en: Our policies forbid the use of advanced AIs. Close the channel.

entries.zh: 我们无法允许人工智能在未监管的状态下运作。摧毁那个舱。
entries.en: We cannot permit an AI to run without surveillance. Fire on that pod.

entries.zh:
§E……

好吧，<<未知访客C>>。您随时可以开始分析。

我——我将继续照顾空降舱。§!
entries.en:
§E...

Very well, <<UNIDENTIFIED VISITOR C>>. You may begin analysis at your convenience.

I -- I will continue to tend to the Drop Pod.§!
Why didn't you call for help?

entries.zh: §E在抵达此处三百一十二年后我关闭了应—急信标。\n\n我收到了一封来自佐勒克辛首星的信息称目标行星无法居住。他们的守护者机器人也陷入了与我相似的境地。我们负责的人无一生还。§!
entries.en: §EI turned off the em--ergency beacon three-hundred-and-twelve years after our arrival here.\n\nI received a message from Xolexin Prime that the target planet was inhospitable. Their Caretaker robots were stuck in a similar situation to me. None of our charges survived.§!

entries.zh: §E那……很合逻辑。愿我的电路可以派上您的用场，<<未知访客>>。请等待。§!
entries.en: §EThat... is logical. May my circuits be of some use to you, <<UNIDENTIFIED VISITOR C>>. Standing by.§!

entries.zh: §E我向您保证，我的程序可以确保在无监管的状态下运行上千年。我的除错能力与故障保险能力是按最长服务寿命设计的，并尽可能缩减任何数据损坏或————§!
entries.en: §EI assure you, I have been programmed to function unattended for thousands of years. My debugging capacities and failsafes have been engineered to provide maximum longevity of service, and to minimize any incidence of data corruption or --- §!

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]在[From.GetName]的轨道上有了惊人的发现。该星球上每单位空间内的量子叠加态数量，超出了至今为止被认为是可能数量的上限。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]提议称[From.GetName]，这颗被[Root.Leader.GetSheHe]命名为$NAME_The_Veil$的星球，同时存在于两个维度：我们的维度，以及另一个未知维度。

不仅如此，星球周围粒子场中的量子态数量仍在稳定增长。目前没有确凿的理论可以解释这一现象。[Root.GetLeaderName]假设灵能——

§H通讯变成了杂讯。§!
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] has made an incredible discovery in orbit of [From.GetName]. The planet possesses a hitherto thought impossible number of superimposed quantum states per unit of space.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] suggests [From.GetName], which [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] codenamed $NAME_The_Veil$, exists simultaneously in two dimensions: our own, and an unknown other.

What is more, the number of quantum states in the particle fields surrounding the planet is increasing at a constant rate. As of yet, there is no confirmed theory that could account for this phenomenon. [Root.GetLeaderName] posits that the psionic energy surr ---

§HThe transmission crackles out to static.§!
What is going on out there?

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]船员为其初次报告被打断而道歉。在通讯中，[phaseshift_planet.GetName]经历了一次彻底的维度转移，它的粒子场旋转进了另一个维度！灵能云团已经消散，显露了一颗宝贵的§Y$pc_gaia$§!。

迷人的是，随着星球的转移，其量子叠加态似乎已被重置，并且正在以星球仍被§Y$pc_shrouded$§!时同等的速度增长。

[Root.GetLeaderName]用量子叠加态的增长速度，以及转移时的量子叠加态总量，推测出星球的转移周期为三个月。或许我们可以设法阻止星球的转移……但首先我们得拥有星系的控制权。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] crew apologizes for the abrupt termination of their initial report. During transmission, [phaseshift_planet.GetName] experienced a complete dimensional phase shift, its particle fields rotating out of one dimension and into another! The cloud of psionic energy has been lifted, revealing a glittering jewel of a §Y$pc_gaia$§!.

Fascinatingly, the number of superimposed quantum states appears to have been reset as the planet shifted, and is now increasing at the same rate as when the planet was a §Y$pc_shrouded$§!.

[Root.GetLeaderName] has used the rate of increase of particle superimposition, and the total number of quantum states at the time of transition to extrapolate a three-month cycle for the planet's dimensional shifts. Perhaps we might develop a method to prevent the planet from shifting... but we should secure the system first.

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]船员为其初次报告被打断而道歉。在通讯中，[phaseshift_planet.GetName]经历了一次彻底的维度转移，它的粒子场旋转进了另一个维度！那颗宝贵的§Y$pc_gaia$§!已经消失，取代而之的是一颗被灵能云团笼罩的旋转星球。

迷人的是，随着星球的转移，其量子叠加态似乎已被重置，并且正在以星球仍是个§Y$pc_gaia$§!时同等的速度增长。

[Root.GetLeaderName]用量子叠加态的增长速度，以及转移时的量子叠加态总量，推测出星球的转移周期为三个月。或许我们可以设法阻止星球的转移……但首先我们得拥有星系的控制权。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] crew apologizes for the abrupt termination of their initial report. During transmission, [phaseshift_planet.GetName] experienced a complete dimensional phase shift, its particle fields rotating out of one dimension and into another! The glittering jewel of a §Y$pc_gaia$§! has vanished, and in its place is now a swirling planet occluded by a shroud of psionic energy.

Fascinatingly, the number of superimposed quantum states appears to have been reset as the planet shifted, and is now increasing at the same rate as when the planet was a §Y$pc_gaia$§!.

[Root.GetLeaderName] has used the rate of increase of particle superimposition, and the total number of quantum states at the time of transition to extrapolate a three-month cycle for the planet's dimensional shifts. Perhaps we might develop a method to prevent the planet from shifting... but we should secure the system first.

[Root.GetName]在[From.GetName]的轨道上有了惊人的发现。该星球上每单位空间内的量子叠加态数量，超出了至今为止被认为是可能数量的上限。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]提议称[From.GetName]，这颗被[Root.Leader.GetSheHe]命名为$NAME_The_Veil$的星球，同时存在于两个维度：我们的维度，以及另一个未知维度。

[Root.GetLeaderName]用量子叠加态的增长速度，以及转移时的量子叠加态总量，推测出星球的转移周期为三个月。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] has made an incredible discovery in orbit of [From.GetName]. The planet possesses a hitherto thought impossible number of superimposed quantum states per unit of space.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] suggests [From.GetName], which [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] codenamed $NAME_The_Veil$, exists simultaneously in two dimensions: our own, and an unknown other.

[Root.GetLeaderName] has used the rate of increase of particle superimposition, and the total number of quantum states at the time of transition to extrapolate a three-month cycle for the planet's dimensional shifts.

entries.zh: [From.GetName]周围的残余能源读数表明，不久之前这颗星球上每单位空间内的量子叠加态数量，超出了至今为止被认为是可能数量的上限。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]提议称[From.GetName]，这颗被[Root.Leader.GetSheHe]命名为$NAME_The_Veil$的星球，同时存在于两个维度：我们的维度，以及另一个未知维度。\n\n该星球已经被锁定在当前的相位维度，应该可以安全地进行殖民。
entries.en: Residual energy readings surrounding [From.GetName] indicate the planet not too long ago possessed a hitherto thought impossible number of superimposed quantum states per unit of space. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] suggests [From.GetName], which [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] codenamed $NAME_The_Veil$, existed simultaneously in two dimensions in the not-too-distant past: our own, and an unknown other.\n\nThe planet has since been locked into its current dimensional phase, and should be considered safe for colonization.

entries.zh: 在六个月的繁杂计算，理论推敲，以及激烈争论之后，[Root.GetName]船员设计了一个方案，可将星球的粒子场锁定在一个正常状态，阻止其在两个维度之间旋转。\n\n一道足够调谐的能源应该可以将[phaseshift_planet.GetName]固定为一个状态，将其锁定为一颗稳定的§Y$pc_gaia$§!。
entries.en: Following six months of number-crunching, theory-busting, and heated debate, the [Root.GetName] crew has devised a method by which the planet's particle fields can be locked into a nominal state, preventing their rotation between dimensions.\n\nA sufficiently tuned pulse of energy should freeze [phaseshift_planet.GetName] in one state, locking it into a stable form as a §Y$pc_gaia$§!.
[phaseshift_planet.GetName] will be permanently transformed into a §Y$pc_gaia$§!.

entries.zh: 转念一想……还是别动它吧。
entries.en: On second thought... leave it be.

entries.zh: 既然[phaseshift_planet.GetName]已经在我们的领地之内，我们应该调查稳定该星球维度波动的可能性。如果我们希望在那颗宝贵的§Y$pc_gaia$§!上殖民，我们必须设法阻止[phaseshift_planet.GetName]每隔三个月就变为§Y$pc_shrouded$§!。
entries.en: Now that [phaseshift_planet.GetName] is within our borders, we should investigate the possibility of stabilizing the planet's state of dimensional flux. If we wish to inhabit the glittering §Y$pc_gaia$§!, we will have to devise a method of preventing [phaseshift_planet.GetName] from phase-shifting back into §Y$pc_shrouded$§! every three months.

entries.zh:
我们在[phaseshift_planet.GetStarName]星系内新获得的星球§Y[phaseshift_planet.GetName]§!展现出了一些非同寻常的特性。它被一种只能称之为灵能的能源所包围，[phaseshift_planet.GetName]每单位空间内的量子叠加态数量，超出了至今为止被认为是可能数量的上限。

每隔三个月，叠加态数量就会达到临界值，使[phaseshift_planet.GetName]经历一次彻底的维度相位转移，它的粒子场将会旋转进另一个维度。该旋转会将一个§Y$pc_shrouded$§!从另一维度转移至我们的维度，然后在下一个周期结束时再次将一个§Y$pc_gaia$§!转移回来。

如果我们希望在那颗宝贵的§Y$pc_gaia$§!上殖民，我们必须设法阻止[phaseshift_planet.GetName]每隔三个月就变为§Y$pc_shrouded$§!。
entries.en:
Our newly acquired planet §Y[phaseshift_planet.GetName]§! in the [phaseshift_planet.GetStarName] system exhibits some incredible properties. Occluded by a strange envelope of what can only be described as psionic energy, [phaseshift_planet.GetName] possesses a hitherto thought impossible number of superimposed quantum states per unit of space.

Every three months, the number of states reaches a critical level, and [phaseshift_planet.GetName] experiences a complete dimensional phase shift, its particle fields rotating out of one dimension and into another. This rotation phases a §Y$pc_shrouded$§! from another dimension into ours, only to phase back a §Y$pc_gaia$§! at the end of the next period.

If we wish to inhabit the glittering §Y$pc_gaia$§!, we will have to devise a method of preventing [phaseshift_planet.GetName] from shifting back into §Y$pc_shrouded$§! every three months.

entries.zh: 那就想办法来相位锁定那颗星球吧。
entries.en: Then let us find a way to phase-lock the planet.

entries.zh: 我们还有更重要的事要处理。
entries.en: We have more important matters to focus on.

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]报告说我们在[phaseshift_planet.GetName]星系内新获得的星球展现出了一些非同寻常的特性。它被一种只能称之为灵能的能源所包围，[phaseshift_planet.GetName]每单位空间内的量子叠加态数量，超出了至今为止被认为是可能数量的上限。

每隔三个月，叠加态数量就会达到临界值，使[phaseshift_planet.GetName]经历一次彻底的维度相位转移，它的粒子场将会旋转进另一个维度。该旋转会将一个§Y$pc_shrouded$§!从另一维度转移至我们的维度，然后在下一个周期结束时再次转移回§Y一颗$pc_gaia$§!。

或许我们可以设法阻止星球的转移……但首先我们得确保该星系的安全。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] reports that the planet [phaseshift_planet.GetName] exhibits some incredible properties. Occluded by a strange envelope of what can only be described as psionic energy, [phaseshift_planet.GetName] possesses a hitherto thought impossible number of superimposed quantum states per unit of space.

Every three months, the number of states reaches a critical level, and [phaseshift_planet.GetName] experiences a complete dimensional phase shift, its particle fields rotating out of one dimension and into another. This rotation phases a §Y$pc_shrouded$§! from another dimension into ours, only to phase back into a §Y$pc_gaia$§! at the end of the next period.

Perhaps we might develop a method to prevent the planet from shifting... but we should secure the system first.

entries.zh:
在对[From.GetName]上覆满植被的建筑进行调查之后，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]发现了它们与栖息在地表上的大量未开化真菌生物之间的可怕关联。

这些建筑似乎是由某种比我们更加先进的文明建造的，用来当作这些真菌生物的有机培养室。此外，这些真菌生物似乎被基因改造成一个用途：作为家畜来填饱其造物主的肚子。

这些生物被[Root.GetLeaderName]命名为[livestock_species.GetName]，是一种思考能力贫乏的温顺生物，这很可能也是其造物主的设计。只需要土壤养分与热量即可存活并繁殖，未来的殖民者们或许可以将它们派上一些用场。
entries.en:
Following investigation of the grown-over structures on [From.GetName], Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has uncovered a grisly connection between them and the vast population of pre-sapient fungoids living on its surface.

It would appear a civilization more technologically advanced than even our own constructed these structures as organic growing chambers for the fungoids. What is more, the fungoids seem to have been genetically tailored and defined to serve one purpose: filling the stomachs of their creator species, as livestock.

The creatures, termed [livestock_species.GetName] by [Root.GetLeaderName], are a docile species largely incapable of complex problem-solving, likely by their creator's design. Requiring only soil nutrition and warmth to survive and procreate, they could potentially be of some use to any future colonists.

entries.zh: 珍贵的有机生物。它们应该得到细心的照顾。
entries.en: Precious organics. They deserve the best pampering.

entries.zh: 同化价值：低于最佳标准。
它们必须被消灭。迟早有一天。
entries.en: They shall be exterminated. All in good time.

entries.zh: 如果不采点儿样品不就太不礼貌了吗。
entries.en: It would be rude not to have a sample.

entries.zh: 既然我们已经在[From.GetName]上殖民，我们得决定该如何处置那些栖息在地表上的未开化真菌生物。\n\n通常情况下，我们关于未开化生物的政策足以在新的殖民地上应对它们。不过，[livestock_species.GetName]看起来确实非常美味。因其非常温顺的天性，将[livestock_species.GetName]们聚集起来赶进处理中心应该不是难事……
entries.en: Now that we have colonized [From.GetName], we should decide what is to be done with the pre-sapient fungoids living on its surface.\n\nIn normal circumstances, our policies regarding pre-sapients would be sufficient in dealing with their presence on our new colony. However, the [livestock_species.GetName]s do look particularly delicious. Due to their incredibly docile nature, it should be relatively easy to round the [livestock_species.GetName]s up into a processing center...

entries.zh: 确实诱人。但我们将遵守我们的规定。
entries.en: Tempting. But we will adhere to our policies.

entries.zh: 将[From.GetName]上的[livestock_species.GetName]聚集到星球上的£building£ §Y$building_livestock_processing_center$§!建筑里（生产：£food£ §Y12§!）。
entries.en: Round up the [livestock_species.GetName] populations on [From.GetName] into a planetside £building£ §Y$building_livestock_processing_center$§! (Produces: £food£ §Y12§!).
Round up the [livestock_species.GetName] populations on [From.GetName] into planetside processor pens. (Produces: £food£ §Y14§!)

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]船成功地从[From.GetStarName]星系里的奇特干扰中分离出了一个信号。信号的内容是一首歌。确切来说，是一首由复杂数学方程式构成的歌，而且[Owner.GetScientistCapital][Root.GetLeaderName]似乎无法不去想它。\n\n是谁或者是什么东西写了这首歌仍不得而知，不过其复杂程度暗示着对子空间和声学的高度精通。信号的测地线表明其来源位于我们的星系之外。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] has succeeded in isolating a signal embedded within the unusual pattern of interference in the [From.GetStarName] system. The signal is a song. A complex sonification of an advanced mathematical equation to be precise, and one that [Owner.GetScientistCapital] [Root.GetLeaderName] cannot seem to get out of their mind.\n\nWho or what may have composed this song remains unknown, though its complexity infers an incredible level of technological sophistication regarding subspace harmonics. The signal's geodesics suggest a point of origin from outside of our galaxy.

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]船员回收了[From.GetName]附近的反射性多面体，并将其带回船上仔细研究。该物体的最有趣的特性就是可以反射大多数向其发射的低频能源波束。高频能源波束则不受影响，使该物体的特性无法用于舰队防御。

尽管对其进行了详尽的调查，[Root.GetName]科研团队仍旧无法判明这个奇特多面体的功能，或是来源。它似乎是空心的，但其类金属表面雕刻着某种科学符号。尽管无法获知该编码数据的完整意义，令人困惑的是，[Root.GetLeaderName]相信它与虫洞度量学有关。

通过研究这些科学符号，我们的科研团队在虫洞理论方面取得了令人兴奋的进展。但这个物体的确切用途仍是个谜。
entries.en:
The [Root.GetName] crew has recovered the reflective polygonal object near [From.GetName], bringing it onboard for detailed study. The object's most intriguing quality is its ability to reflect most types of low-frequency energy beams directed toward it. High-frequency energy beams, however, remain unaffected, making the object's properties useless with regards to any potential fleet defense applications.

Despite extensive examination, the [Root.GetName] research team has been unable to determine the function, or origin, of this peculiar polygon. It appears to be hollow, but its metalloid surface is engraved with some kind of scientific notation. Though the full meaning of this codified data eludes us, [Root.GetLeaderName] believes it relates to wormhole metrics.

Our research team was able to glean some fascinating insights into wormhole theory by studying these notations. Whatever purpose this object was created for, however, is still a mystery.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]船员报告称，在[From.GetName]星系附近发现了腐朽的轨道空间站与多个死寂星球。某个曾殖民于[From.GetName]星系的星际文明似乎很久以前就毁灭了。[ratling_planet_tar.GetName]星球简直就像个垃圾场，上面满是辐射弥漫且锈迹斑斑的建筑废墟，基础设施与载具。未侦测到高等生命的存在。\n\n我们或许可以勘察该星系与邻近星系中的类似星球，来获知更多关于这一失落文明的情报。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] crew have reported the presence of decaying orbital stations and multiple tomb worlds near the [From.GetName] system. Whatever interstellar nation once inhabited the [From.GetName] system appears to have collapsed into ruin long ago. [ratling_planet_tar.GetName] is a junkyard of a planet, covered in the irradiated, rusting remnants of demolished buildings, infrastructure and vehicles. No higher forms of life are recognizable.\n\nWe might gain more insight into this lost civilization by surveying any similar planets in this and neighboring systems.

entries.zh: 如果还有活的，必须将其消灭。
entries.en: If any remain, they will be exterminated.

entries.zh:
正如[Root.GetName]船员的初步猜想，[From.GetName]似乎是那个有遨游太空能力的帝国的首都，其前殖民地现在已是死寂星球上的充满辐射的废墟。

从团队收集的数据看来，几乎可以确定是一场对未知外部威胁发动的星际战争，导致了这个失落文明的陨落。我们仍不确定星球的主人是击退了攻击者但毁于战后的辐射尘，还是攻击者消灭了这些殖民地及其居民并扬长而去。

因废墟的极端环境使我们无法从残留的电子器件中提取数据，而其首都和其它殖民地中也没有任何生还者，这似乎将成为不解之谜。
entries.en:
As per the [Root.GetName] crew's initial suspicions, [From.GetName] appears to be the fallen capital of the space-faring society whose former colonies are now but irradiated scrap heaps on inhospitable tomb worlds.

From the data the team has gathered, the downfall of this lost civilization was almost certainly the result of interstellar warfare waged against some unknown, external threat. It remains unclear whether the planet's owners repelled the invasion but succumbed to the post-war fallout of a pyrrhic victory, or if the invaders crushed these colonies and their inhabitants before moving on.

As the extreme state of ruin on the planet precludes the extraction of data from any remaining electronics, and neither the capital nor its colonies possess any survivors, it seems we may never know for certain.

entries.zh:
[Root.Capital.GetName]收到了关于[notif_planet.GetStarName]星系中的[notif_planet.GetName]曾被以为是不毛之地的情报。我们的勘探者曾以为是无法居住的废墟星球，事实上住着一群像老鼠一般的智慧生物！

它们被命名为“$NAME_Ketlings$”，这些生物一直隐居在巨大废墟中的隧道里，使我们无法察觉。一定是这些巨大垃圾堆的复杂结构与惊人密度，阻挡了我们的扫描仪深入其中。

是什么使得$NAME_Ketlings$来到地面仍不得而知，不过我们现在既然观察它们，我们注意到它们的科技几乎完全基于行星废墟中的破旧垃圾。

难道$NAME_Ketlings$是创造了这些废墟的失落星际文明的最后幸存者吗？深入研究或许可以一探究竟。
entries.en:
Intelligence reports are coming in to [Root.Capital.GetName] regarding the hitherto lifeless surface of [notif_planet.GetName] in the [notif_planet.GetStarName] system. What our surveyors initially considered an uninhabited junk pile of a planet is, in fact, home to a species of rat-like sapients!

Dubbed "$NAME_Ketlings$," these creatures had been living hidden from our view in tunnels in the planet's enormous scrap piles. The complex composition and incredible density of these massive junkheaps must have hindered earlier penetration by our scanners.

Whatever may have brought the $NAME_Ketlings$ to the surface is thus far unknown, though now that we can observe them, we have noted their technology is almost entirely based on repurposed junk from the planetary ruins they inhabit.

Could the $NAME_Ketlings$ be the last survivors of the lost interstellar civilization who made these ruins? Closer study may yield more information.

entries.zh:
[Root.GetLeaderName]对[From.From.GetName]上的鼠形智慧生物的调查产生了惊人的结论。这些$NAME_Ketlings$是灵能体，可以通过横跨数百万小型个体的巨大心灵感应网络来共享思维。尽管它们似乎避免与我们接触，而我们也没有发现它们拥有先进太空科技的证据，但将$NAME_Ketlings$归类为原始生物却非常不妥。事实上，它们的某些改造机械的技术复杂程度甚至逼近我们的水平。

此外，$NAME_Ketlings$既不是这些城市的建造者的后代，也不是将其摧毁的征服者。$NAME_Ketlings$的祖先，其实是被当初定居此地的星际文明当作宠物的动物！在其主人陨落后，原始$NAME_Ketlings$是在这些废墟星球上持续数个世纪的辐射尘中存活下来的少数生物之一。

长期暴露在辐射中加速了$NAME_Ketlings$的基因突变，而其灵活的肢体，相对较高的初始智力，并且更接近废弃工具，这些因素导致了一个高科技帝国的迅速发展。
entries.en:
[Root.GetLeaderName]'s investigation into the rat-like sapients on [From.From.GetName] has produced some surprising results. The $NAME_Ketlings$ are psions, capable of sharing their thoughts via a telepathic network spanning millions of small minds. Though they avoid interacting with us, and we lack evidence to suggest they are capable of advanced spaceflight, it would be remiss to classify the $NAME_Ketlings$ as mere primitives. In fact, some of their repurposed machinery possesses a technical sophistication approaching even our own.

Moreover, the $NAME_Ketlings$ are neither the descendants of the civilization that constructed these cities, nor the conquerors that destroyed them. Rather, the $NAME_Ketlings$ were once the pets of the spacefarers who first colonized these systems! After their masters' downfall, the proto-$NAME_Ketlings$ were one of the few species to survive centuries of nuclear fallout on these ruined planets.

Constant exposure to radioactive elements led to faster mutations in the $NAME_Ketlings$' genetic code, and their nimble appendages, relative starting intelligence, and close proximity to a variety of decrepit tools all culminated in the rapid emergence of a technologically advanced culture.

entries.zh: 我们已经成功的从奇怪的垃圾堆住民$NAME_Ketlings$手中占领了[From.From.GetName]。我们将根据物种政策来处理行星上剩余的$NAME_Ketlings$。\n\n我们不确定我们的入侵会让它们其他星球上的同伴做出什么样的反应……但是能有多糟？
entries.en: We have successfully conquered [From.From.GetName] from the curious junk-dwelling $NAME_Ketlings$. The $NAME_Ketlings$ remaining planetside will be dealt with according to the species policies we have outlined for them.\n\nWe are uncertain what kind of reaction our intrusion might prompt from their comrades on other planets... but how bad could it be?

entries.zh: 我们成功地从奇特的垃圾居民$NAME_Ketlings$手中征服了[From.From.GetName]。\n\n这些奇特的垃圾居民$NAME_Ketlings$将被吸收进[Root.GetName]。
entries.en: We have successfully conquered [From.From.GetName] from the curious junk-dwelling $NAME_Ketlings$.\n\nThe curious junk-dwelling $NAME_Ketlings$ will be absorbed into the [Root.GetName].

entries.zh: 我们已经成功的从奇怪的垃圾堆住民$NAME_Ketlings$手中占领了[From.From.GetName]。我们将根据物种政策来处理行星上剩余的$NAME_Ketlings$。\n\n残存的$NAME_Ketlings$将被发射至太空中。
entries.en: We have successfully conquered [From.From.GetName] from the last of the junk-dwelling $NAME_Ketlings$. The $NAME_Ketlings$ remaining planetside will be dealt with according to the species policies we have outlined for them.\n\nThe final remnants of $NAME_Ketlings$ autonomy will be dispersed into the void.

entries.zh: 我们成功地从奇特的垃圾居民$NAME_Ketlings$手中征服了[From.From.GetName]。\n\n最后残余的奇特$NAME_Ketlings$将被吸收进[Root.GetName]。
entries.en: We have successfully conquered [From.From.GetName] from the last of the junk-dwelling $NAME_Ketlings$.\n\nThe final remnants of the curious $NAME_Ketlings$ will be absorbed into the [Root.GetName].

entries.zh: 传感器在[sensor_ratling_system.GetName]星系中突然发现了大量活动迹象。先前遭遇的$NAME_Ketlings$发射了一队可超光速旅行的战舰，而地面侦查表明其居住的巨大垃圾堆其实隐藏了广阔的复合矿场，发电厂，菌类农场，以及地下科研设施。\n\n尽管十分惊人，它们的船到目前为止尚未表露出敌意，并且$NAME_Ketlings$很可能只是在其边境设防而已。无论如何，现在明显该将这些外星人视为一个真正的帝国了。
entries.en: Sensors report a sudden burst of activity in the [sensor_ratling_system.GetName] System. The previously encountered $NAME_Ketlings$ have launched a fleet of FTL-capable warships, and planetside reconnaissance indicates the enormous junkheaps that made up their homes in fact concealed extensive mining networks, power plants, fungus-farms, and subterranean research facilities.\n\nWhile alarming, their ships have thus far made no display of hostile intent, and it is quite possible the $NAME_Ketlings$ are merely establishing defenses along their borders. Nevertheless, it is clearly time to recognize these aliens as an empire in their own right.

entries.zh: 过去的42年零3天里，位于[Root.Capital.GetName]的研究人员一直怀着热烈的期望观察着我们在[From.From.From.GetName]发现的原子钟进行的倒计时。\n\n几十年来的猜测与疑惑在瞬间烟消云散：随着原子钟倒数归零，他发射了一群可自我复制的纳米机器人！
entries.en: Researchers on [Root.Capital.GetName] have eagerly anticipated the countdown of the mysterious atomic clock of prodigious precision found on [From.From.From.GetName] for the past 42 years and 3 days.\n\nSeveral decades' worth of heated speculation and conjecture have evaporated in an instant: the clock has just now reached its momentous deadline, ejecting a stream of self-replicating nanites!

entries.zh:
$distar.311.desc.base$

根据计算，这群纳米机器人的抛物线对准的是[atomic_clock_planet.GetStarName]星系中的另一颗行星，[atomic_clock_planet.GetName]，预计将在一个月内抵达。

它们到达后将会发生什么，我们尚不得而知……
entries.en:
$distar.311.desc.base$

These nanites are streaming on a trajectory towards another planet in the [atomic_clock_planet.GetStarName] System, [atomic_clock_planet.GetName], projected to arrive within the month.

Whatever may happen once they arrive remains to be seen...

entries.zh: 有什么消息及时通知我们。
纳米机器人群着陆后，会立即发布情况更新。
entries.en: An update will be issued as soon as the nanite stream makes planetfall.

entries.zh: 绝不能接受。对这群纳米机器人开火！
命令我们处于该星系中的人手，摧毁从原子钟里出现的纳米机器人群。
entries.en: Order our crew in the system to destroy the nanite stream being emitted from the atomic clock.

entries.zh:
[atomic_clock_planet.GetStarName]星系小行星带中弹射而出的纳米机器人群，在[atomic_clock_planet.GetName]着陆了！这群纳米机器人以惊人速度迅速繁殖，只用了几个小时便覆盖了整颗行星的表面，并开始对其进行环境改造，将其转化为§Y盖亚星球§!！

环境改造完成后几小时，所有参与改造纳米机器人全部自动关闭，并且腐烂至无法辨识的地步，直接导致我们无法从中提取任何信息与情报。

然而，它们的残留物为这个已经变得十分吸引人的星球表面增添了不少价值可观的金属合成物。
entries.en:
The nanite stream ejected by the atomic clock in the [atomic_clock_planet.GetStarName] system asteroid belt has made planetfall on [atomic_clock_planet.GetName]! Replicating at an incredible rate, the nanites covered the entire surface of the planet in a period of hours, proceeding to terraform it into a §YGaia World§!!

Hours after the completion of the terraforming event, the nanites involved in the process deactivated and decayed beyond recognition, leaving us with little ability to extract any information from them.

However, their remains have peppered the surface of the now-very-tempting planet with valuable metallic composites.

entries.zh:
据我们正在观察[atomic_clock_planet.GetStarName]星系的军官称，虽然大部分流向[atomic_clock_planet.GetName]的纳米机器人群已被炮火摧毁，却还是有数量难以统计的仍处于活跃状态纳米机器人到达了该行星表面。

它们的目的至今尚不明确，不过自从着陆后，它们就开始以一种似乎随机的方式开始了疾速繁殖。

[atomic_clock_planet.GetName]现在已被这种能够自我复制的显微级物质构成的粘液覆盖了。
entries.en:
Our military officers observing the [atomic_clock_planet.GetStarName] System report that while the vast majority of the nanites streaming towards [atomic_clock_planet.GetName] were fired upon and destroyed, an undetectable quantity of still-active nanites managed to reach the planet's surface.

Whatever purpose they were meant for remains unknown, but once reaching the planet's surface they have begun to replicate rapidly in a seemingly random fashion.

[atomic_clock_planet.GetName] is now covered in a moving slurry of microscopic replicators.

entries.zh:
$distar.311.desc.base$

纳米机器人把这颗小行星变化成了一艘十分神奇的无人军事舰船，随后便离开了小行星的表面。

如果有兴趣，我们完全可以将其据为己有。
entries.en:
$distar.311.desc.base$

These nanites left the surface of the asteroid, where they have coalesced into a fascinating, unmanned military vessel.

It is ours for the taking, should we so desire.

entries.zh:
$distar.311.desc.base$

纳米机器人在[From.From.From.GetName]表面建造了某种高级的计算网络。网络目前处于关闭状态，似乎也没有任何人工智能存在的迹象，而纳米机器人在建造完成后也都自动关闭了。

我们的研究人员对于这个网络的存在目的感到十分疑惑。要想研究这玩意，估计够让他们忙上好一阵了。
entries.en:
$distar.311.desc.base$

The nanites have constructed some manner of advanced computational network on the surface of [From.From.From.GetName]. The network is inactive, and seemingly devoid of any AI, the nanites having deactivated the instant its construction was complete.

Our researchers are somewhat baffled as to the purpose of the network. Studying it should keep them occupied for quite some time.

entries.zh: 感染了某种神秘疾病后，这些殖民者产生了敌意。
entries.en: Afflicted with a mysterious condition, these colonists have turned hostile.

entries.zh: 当这个环形世界仍然是废墟的时候，有几百个外星克隆生物被封存在冷冻保存仓之中。现在这些被修复的冷冻仓成为了一所纪念碑。
entries.en: Hundreds of alien clones were left sealed in cryostasis chambers when this Ring World was still a ruin. Now fully restored, the clones have been preserved in this monument.

entries.zh: 这座星球上有片十三公里见方的区域，散布着起源未知的遗迹，以及许多古怪而独特的异星造物。令人困惑的是，它同时也使到访者产生心满意足的情绪。
entries.en: A thirteen-by-thirteen kilometer stretch of land on this planet is a ruin of unknown origin, littered with many bizarre and unique alien artifacts. Bafflingly, it also produces sensations of deep contentment in its visitors.

entries.zh: 一堆锈迹斑斑且辐射弥漫的崩塌基础设施、建筑废墟，以及腐朽残骸，源自一个未知的文明。
entries.en: A rusting, irradiated jumble of collapsed infrastructure, destroyed buildings, and decaying wreckage from an unknown civilization.

entries.zh: 原属于这座星球的真菌生物被基因改造得天性温顺……并且美味。这座处理中心会将其养肥，然后收割。
entries.en: The fungoids native to this planet were genetically engineered to be docile... and delicious. This processing center nourishes, then harvests them.

entries.zh: 入侵这颗星球的外来真菌像癌细胞一般疯狂扩散，毁坏了地形并干扰基础设施。
entries.en: The exofungus that has invaded this planet spreads like a cancer, choking the terrain and interfering with infrastructure.

entries.zh: 初步报告显示§Y[From.GetName]§!上的海洋从某种程度上来说居然是活的，其中包含着一种我们从来都没见过的外星实体。\n\n我们应当建立一座低轨研究前哨来研究将这片活体海洋。我们预期可以获得进展。
entries.en: Preliminary reports suggest the ocean covering §Y[From.GetName]§! is somehow alive, comprising an alien entity unlike any we've encountered before.\n\nWe should establish a low-orbit research outpost to study the living sea. Updates are to be expected.

entries.zh: 研究居住在三个相连星系中的垃圾堆隧道里的奇特智慧生物，或许可以更加了解这个曾经拥有这些星球的星际文明。
entries.en: Studying the strange sapients that live in tunnels in the junk heaps of three linked systems might yield insight into the lost interstellar civilization that once ruled these worlds.

entries.zh: 这些是一个失落文明的残骸，当超强耀斑耗尽了星球大气层时像烛火一样被掐灭了。
entries.en: There are remnants of a lost civilization on this planet, snuffed out like a candle when solar superflares depleted the planet's atmosphere.

entries.zh: 这颗恒星偶尔会射出超强耀斑，向星系中喷发大量等离子。
entries.en: This star exhibits occasional superflares, ejecting huge quantities of plasma into the system.

entries.zh: 我们知道这颗星球的恒星会喷发超强耀斑，可能会对星球表面的生命与电子器件带来有害影响。
entries.en: This planet's sun is known to exhibit massive superflares, which may have adverse effects for life and electronics on the planet's surface.

entries.zh: 这颗星球受到了超强耀斑的影响，导致辐射水平上升以及电子器件受到干扰。
entries.en: This planet has been affected by a solar superflare, resulting in increased radiation levels and electronic interference.

entries.zh: 这座星球的人们受到防护，免受超强耀斑活动的负面影响。
entries.en: This planet's populace is shielded from the harmful effects of its sun's superflare activity.

entries.zh: 围绕这座黑洞的吸积盘具有很高的电荷，产生了大量静电能源。
entries.en: The accretion disk surrounding this black hole is highly charged, generating significant quantities of electrostatic energy.

entries.zh: 一支神秘的舰队进入了这个黑洞的视界线，外界观测者只能看到它们在表面上留下的永远的身影。
entries.en: A mysterious fleet entered this black hole's event horizon, leaving their image forever suspended on its surface for outside observers.

entries.zh: 这座星球上仍有初级机器人在活动，而创造它们的文明早已消逝。
entries.en: There are ancient robots still functioning on this planet, left behind when the civilization that created them perished.

entries.zh: 该人员正在表现出奇怪且有时的行为。
entries.en: This population is exhibiting strange, sometimes violent behavior.

entries.zh: 该成员坚信我们是重生之圣者的信使。因此，他们非常渴望能够取悦我们。
entries.en: This population believes us to be messengers from their god of rebirth. As such, their eagerness to please us is remarkable.

entries.zh: 一种会使感染者混乱并产生侵略性的神经病毒，使这颗星球上的社会科学家蒙受了损失。
entries.en: A neurological virus causing confusion and aggression in infected patients has decimated the ranks of our societal researchers on this planet.

entries.zh: 在环绕这颗恒星的废弃环形世界上，有成百上千个克隆体封存在冷冻舱中。
entries.en: There are hundreds of clones sealed in cryostasis chambers on the ruined Ring World surrounding this star.

entries.zh: 这颗月球的表面上有一只未知巨大外星生物的遗骸。
entries.en: The enormous corpse of an unidentified alien creature rests upon the surface of this moon.

entries.zh: 某种巨型外星生物的遗骸默默地在轨道上守望着这颗星球。
entries.en: The corpse of some gargantuan alien creature keeps silent vigil in orbit over this planet.

entries.zh: 这颗星球上的有机生命正受到某种神秘现象的影响。
entries.en: Organic lifeforms on this planet are being affected by some yet-unexplained phenomenon.

entries.zh: 一个活动的电脉冲网络交织在这颗小行星的表面上。
entries.en: A living network of electrical impulses crisscrosses the surface of this planetoid.

entries.zh: 我们发现了一颗气态巨行星，它包含上万亿公升的酯，其成分与我们祖先数千年来一直酿造的酒精饮料相同。人们为此而欢呼雀跃。
entries.en: The discovery of a gas giant possessing billions upon billions of liters of an ester identical to one distilled into inebriants by our ancestors for thousands of years has led to widespread gaiety among our citizens.

entries.zh: 这颗星球地壳构造中共鸣水晶的频率，对我们物种具有医疗效果。
entries.en: The resonant crystals that line this planet's tectonic crust resonate at a medically therapeutic frequency for our species.

entries.zh: 这颗星球的磁场共鸣频率对我们的神经网络非常有益。
entries.en: This planet's magnetosphere resonates at a frequency very conducive to our neural network.

entries.zh: 一种可在极端环境繁殖的外来真菌像癌细胞一般疯狂扩散，覆盖了地貌。
entries.en: An extremophilic exofungus spreads on this planet like a cancer, choking the terrain.

entries.zh: 这颗星球的海面下存在某种类人猿集体的遗迹，从南极一路延伸至北极。
entries.en: The ruins of an ancient arthropoid collective stretch from pole to pole on this planet, long-buried beneath its waves.

entries.zh: 以其尺寸而言，这艘机器人战舰的外壳非常坚固。
entries.en: The robotic warship's construction boasts an unusually resilient hull for its size.

entries.zh: 这颗星球上的人们怀疑其同胞们选择与神经蛞蝓共生。
entries.en: This planet's populace has misgivings about their fellow colonists choosing to enter into symbiotic union with neural slugs.

entries.zh: 我们近来的神经蛞蝓共生在这个星球上引起了不适的问题。
entries.en: This world is having issues acclimatizing to our recent symbiosis with neural slugs.

entries.zh: 这颗星球上到处都是凶恶的巨型植物，给了我们研究的机会，但对居民来说也是个危险的阻碍。
entries.en: Vicious megaflora dominates this planet's landscape, creating opportunities for research, but also dangerous obstacles for any inhabitants.

entries.zh: 尽管我们尚未得知这颗星球的海洋的本质，但不知为何，它毫无疑问是活的。接触到它的有机生命体的思维中，会涌现出思想、幻象和冲动，宛如柔和的歌声在心海中起舞。
entries.en: Though the nature of this planet's sea eludes us, it is somehow, unquestionably, alive. Thoughts, visions, and impulses like soft songs dance in the minds of organic beings who come into contact with it.

entries.zh: 拾荒者并非按照任何明确的现成图纸而造。因此，其摇摇欲坠的构造中包含一些结构弱点。任何知晓这些弱点的舰队都可以利用它们。
entries.en: The Scavenger was not built on any pre-engineered design. As a result, its ramshackle construction contains a number of structural weaknesses. Any fleet made aware of them could exploit this.

entries.zh: 远古缇扬奇族母的甲壳上有个弱点，就是一枚镶入其外皮中的尚未爆炸的巨型质子鱼雷。我们的舰队知道该如何引爆它。
entries.en: There is a chink in the ancient Tiyanki Matriarch's armor, in the form of a massive unexploded proton torpedo lodged in her hide. Our fleets know how to detonate it.

entries.zh: 对拾荒者机器人的伤害
这颗星球定期在维度之间转移，反复从一颗§Y$pc_shrouded$§!与一颗§Y$pc_gaia$§!之间来回变换。当这种转移发生时，上面的居民会发生什么事仍不得而知。
entries.en: This planet shifts between dimensions on a regular period: transforming from a §Y$pc_shrouded$§! to a §Y$pc_gaia$§! and back again. It is unknown what might happen to any settlers on its surface when such a shift occurs.

entries.zh: $TRIGGER_FAIL$§R无法殖民正在维度间相移的星球。§!
entries.en: $TRIGGER_FAIL$§RCan't colonize worlds that are phase-shifting between dimensions.§!

entries.zh: 来自这个星系的小行星带中一个被封锁的原子钟的一群纳米机器人在这里建造了一个目的不明的计算网络。
entries.en: A computational network of unknown purpose was constructed here by a stream of nanites that emerged from a sealed atomic clock found in the system's asteroid belt.

entries.zh: 这座荒废的空间站经历了数个世纪的残骸撞击，漂浮在这颗星球的轨道上。
entries.en: Scarred by centuries of debris impacts, a dilapidated relic of a station trails a weary path around this planet.

entries.zh: 一座废弃的空间站在这座虫洞中间慢慢旋转。
entries.en: An abandoned station spins in slow circles at the mouth of this wormhole.

entries.zh: 一艘满载容器的废弃舰船盘旋在这颗星球的低轨道上。
entries.en: A derelict ship laden with tanks hangs in low orbit of this planet.

entries.zh: 一只空降舱在宇宙里漂流，它原本运载的外星人早已变成干瘪的空壳。
entries.en: A castoff drop pod floats through space, the aliens it was transporting now but withered husks within.

entries.zh: 一只空降舱在宇宙里漂流。我们侦测到里面有微弱的活动迹象。
entries.en: A castoff drop pod floats through space. We are registering faint activity from within.

entries.zh: 一台专司照顾他人的机器。过去的失败深深地印刻在其记忆库里。
entries.en: A machine specialized in caring for others. The failures of the past are embedded in its memory banks.

entries.zh: 确保营养物质充足，工作环境整洁，受监护者得到适当刺激，这些都在守护者的职责范围之下。
entries.en: Ensuring nutrients are available, that the workspace is clean, and that the wards are properly stimulated all fall under the purview of a Caretaker.

entries.zh: 我们获得了守护者的独特知识。
entries.en: The unique knowledge of the Caretaker has become our own.

entries.zh: §L温顺而又美味！这个物种因其被改造了高级脑部机能而成为一种无害的牲畜，可以自我照料，且免受社交与自我决定的繁琐。§!
entries.en: §LDocile and delicious, this species has had its higher brain functions genetically altered to create a kind of harmless livestock that can care for itself, without the pesky need for social interaction or self-determination.§!

entries.zh: §L这个物种正享受着与神经共生体的共存：一种良性蛞蝓附着于宿主的脑干上。§!
entries.en: §LThis species is enjoying the presence of a neural symbiont: a helpful slug that attaches itself to the brain stem of its host.§!

entries.zh: 这位领袖正因神经共生体而受益：一种附在宿主脑干上的有益蛞蝓。
entries.en: This leader is enjoying the presence of a neural symbiont: a helpful slug that attaches itself to the brain stem of its host.

entries.zh: 当面对战争时，这位领袖无情地狂热，而且坚定不移。
entries.en: When it comes to warfare, this leader is mercilessly obsessive, and singular in purpose.

entries.zh: §L该物种经过改造，略微提高了其环境适应性，可以忍耐更加严酷的气候。§!
entries.en: §LThis species has been modified to be slightly more adaptive and can now better endure harsh climates.§!

entries.zh: §L该物种经过改造，变得更加适应拥挤的群居生活。§!
entries.en: §LThis species has been modified to be more social and accepting of crowded conditions.§!

entries.zh: §L该物种经过改造，使其伤口愈合得更快，不仅战斗力更强，同时也稍微延长了寿命。§!
entries.en: §LThis species has been modified to heal faster, making them more dangerous in battle and somewhat longer-lived in general.§!

entries.zh: 在拾荒者机器人的残骸里发现了一种高效的船壳自动维修系统，由数十亿个微型纳米机器人组成，并已改造成可为我们所用。至于拾荒者是从远古残骸中夺取了这个系统，还是原本就自带该系统则不得而知。
entries.en: A highly effective hull auto-repair system comprised of billions of microscopic nanomachines was found among the smoking remains of the Scavenger, and has been repurposed for our uses. Whether the Scavenger pilfered this system from an ancient derelict, or was originally constructed with it remains unknown.

entries.zh: 当适应了一个物种的基因组之后，这种经工程设计出来的组织能够表现出强烈的神经再生特性，显著加速了其受体中神经元、轴突和突触的发育。
entries.en: When tailored to a species' genome, this form of tissue engineering has intensive neuroregenerative properties, significantly increasing the development of neurons, axons, and synapses in its recipient.

entries.zh: 极度先进的自动火炮，射出的弹药可以在接近目标时引爆成一片纳米机器人云，以此过载目标的护盾并蚕食其船体区段。
entries.en: Highly advanced autocannons capable of ejecting shells that explode into a cloud of nanites at the target, overwhelming shields and chewing through hull sections.

entries.zh: 在现有的设计上，改装以纳米机器人的筒状战斗部，可以对舰载机大快朵颐，可谓是舰载机飞行员的噩梦。
entries.en: Improving upon previous designs by launching canisters of nanites capable of eating away at strike craft, these flak batteries are the bane of any fighter pilot.

entries.zh: 缇扬奇族母的外皮因岁月与未知生物过程而硬化。
entries.en: The hide of the Tiyanki Matriarch has been hardened by the years and unknown biological processes.

entries.zh: 我们的公民为成功殖民天堂星球而欢呼。
entries.en: Our citizens rejoice now that we have finally colonized the paradisaical planet Paridayda.

entries.zh: 一个仿佛仙境般的美丽世界。
entries.en: A paradisaical world of unparalleled beauty.

entries.zh: 我们有一只碉堡机器人在协助我们的工程部门。
entries.en: We have a bunker-bot aiding our engineering department.

entries.zh: 一本外星星系漫游指南激发了人们对未知的热爱。
entries.en: An alien hitchhiker's guide to the galaxy has inspired our people's love for the unknown.
An Alien Guide to the Galaxy

entries.zh: 一个游手好闲并乱丢垃圾的不利因素
太阳能动力的远古收割机在协助收割星球上的庄稼。
entries.en: Ancient solar-powered harvesters assist in gathering the planet's crops.

entries.zh: 该星球受到异常地震现象的影响。
entries.en: This world is afflicted by abnormal seismological phenomena.

entries.zh: 剧毒黏液与气体不断从星球表面的裂隙中渗出。整个星球上都弥漫着一股臭鸡蛋的味道。
entries.en: Toxic slime and gases seep from the deep rifts stretching across the planet's surface. The entire planet reeks of rotten egg.

entries.zh: 这里存在有毒的化学溶剂与被溶解的有机物质，使这片区域无法居住。
entries.en: A noxious slush of chemical solvents and dissolved organic matter make this area uninhabitable.

entries.zh: 地震现象使星球地壳开裂，喷出硫磺气体与毒性粘液。
entries.en: Seismological phenomena are causing the planet crust to crack, spewing out sulfuric gases and toxic slime.

entries.zh: 从维克塔·泽沃尼亚号的导航设备中提取的坐标指向这个位置。
entries.en: The coordinates extracted from the Vechtar Zavonia's navigational drive point to this location.

entries.zh: 数颗恒星开始异常地悸动。
entries.en: Several stars have begun to pulsate in an unusual manner.

entries.zh: 阿兹詹虫是巨大的凶猛蛞蝓，可以碾碎其敌人，并分泌一种黏性液体。
entries.en: The Azizians make titanic murderous slugs, crushing their foes, secreting a sticky fluid.

entries.zh: 虚空孳孽的卵进化出了通过吸收邻近恒星的能源来忍受严酷太空环境的能力。
entries.en: Voidspawn eggs have evolved to withstand the harsh conditions of space by absorbing and conserving energy from their nearest star.

entries.zh: 一个早已消逝的外星物种的巨型世代舰船，其导航设备中可能藏有一颗完美星球的坐标。
entries.en: A massive generation ship belonging to a long dead race of aliens may hold the encrypted location of a utopian planet within its navigational drive.

entries.zh: 只要发射一个探测器，我们就将最终揭开谜底：眼前这颗毫无生机的荒芜行星是否就是马达科-沃尔传说中的天堂。
entries.en: Sending a probe to the planet's surface will allow us to decide once and for all whether the desolate barren world that lies before us is in fact all that remains of the Mardak Vol's mythical paradise.

entries.zh: 一座废弃的外星平台漂浮在[star_lifting_star.GetName]的轨道上。如果我们能设法修复它，可是我们改善并利用恒星提供的能源。
entries.en: A decrepit platform of ancient alien design orbits [star_lifting_star.GetName]. If we could find a way to repair it, it would allow us to improve and harness the star's energy outflow.

entries.zh: 一座废弃的外星平台漂浮在[star_lifting_star.GetName]的轨道上。它有一些非常实验性的微波束科技，有改造成武器的潜力。
entries.en: A decrepit platform of ancient alien design orbits [star_lifting_star.GetName]. It has some highly experimental microwave beam technology with potential for weaponization.

entries.zh: 位于[big_rip_planet.GetName]轨道上的废弃观测站的数据储存装置已被清空。我们必须派人到星球上去，才能弄明白这里原先居住的智慧生物出了什么事。
entries.en: The data storage units on the observation post orbiting [big_rip_planet.GetName] have been wiped. We will have to send a team planetside if we want to get to the bottom of what happened to the intelligent lifeforms previously inhabiting the planet.

entries.zh: 我们发现了一颗金属小方块，每一面都有不同的颜色，令科学专员[cube_science_officer.GetName]大感困惑，认为它里面一定藏着什么有价值的东西。
entries.en: The discovery of a tiny metal cube with different colored sides has mystified Science Officer [cube_science_officer.GetName], who is certain it hides something of value inside.

entries.zh: 星系中有数颗恒星开始奇怪地悸动。船员们担心这些读数是仪器故障造成的，但科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]想要详细调查其中一颗恒星。
entries.en: Several stars in the galaxy have begun to pulsate oddly. The crew have raised concerns that these readings were caused by a sensory malfunction, but officer [Root.GetLeaderName] would like to investigate one of the stars more closely.

entries.zh: 我们在[From.GetName]上收集了用于测试的外星武器残骸，以供分析。
entries.en: We have gathered the remains of alien weaponry used in extensive weapon testing on [From.GetName] for analysis.

entries.zh: 虚空孳孽的卵进化出了通过吸收邻近恒星的能源来忍受严酷太空环境的能力。或许这些碎片可以揭露它的秘密。
entries.en: Somehow the Voidspawn egg has evolved to survive the harsh conditions of space, by absorbing and conserving huge amounts of solar energy. Maybe the remains of the shattered shards could reveal its secrets.

entries.zh: 在[time_loop_world.GetName]上保护着有鳞族智慧文明的远古护盾正因热量与缺乏修理而开裂。我们必须修复它。
entries.en: The ancient shield enclosing the sapient squamate civilization on [time_loop_world.GetName] is cracking from heat and disrepair. We must restore it.

entries.zh: 我们准备了一个打断时空循环的计划。
entries.en: We have prepared a project to interrupt the time loop.

entries.zh: 一个未知的废弃外星平台正围绕一颗恒星漫无目的地漂浮。
entries.en: An abandoned platform of unknown alien design is drifting aimlessly around a star.

entries.zh: 这座恒星平台通过用微波轰击其大气层来增加恒星的太阳风流出量。这些太阳风的能量随后可以被开采。
